<query>I noticed the trainer at work only adjusts his broom when he’s near me, like he wants to impress me silently. Can someone’s body language really reveal feelings they won’t admit? Sometimes I feel like I’m the only one who catches these little signs of secret admiration.</query>
<response>Yes, body language often reveals emotions or intentions that people may not explicitly state. Subtle gestures, like adjusting tools when near someone, can stem from subconscious habits—such as a desire to appear competent, engage in conversation, or even signal interest. While it’s possible the trainer’s actions are unintentional or routine, repeated patterns (like focusing on you specifically) might indicate admiration or a wish to connect. However, context matters: is this behavior exclusive to you, or part of their general demeanor? Trust your instincts, but also consider that people often act on habit or social cues without deeper meaning. If curiosity persists, observe for other signs (eye contact, willingness to engage) before drawing conclusions. You’re not alone in noticing these nuances—many people pick up on subtle signals, even if they don’t always act on them.</response>
